Sodium bicarbonate acts as a buffer in the extracellular fluid, increasing its pH and buffering capacity. During intense exercise, muscles produce hydrogen ions (H⁺), which contribute to acidosis and fatigue.  
A higher extracellular buffering capacity allows H⁺ to move more readily from the muscle into the extracellular space, delaying the drop in intramuscular pH and maintaining performance longer.  

That matches the description in option (A).  

Final answer: (A)
